title: At the coffee shop: what would you like
goal: Order food and drinks politely — and understand why the word for "want" in Egyptian isn't a verb but an adjective that changes with the person.
bekal: order at a coffee shop or restaurant at three levels of politeness
use عايز، عاوزة، عايزين in the right form
use ممكن to ask for something without sounding bossy

dialogs.title: حوار — على القهوة
dialogs.intro: Late afternoon at an *ahwa* — a Cairo street café with wooden chairs on the sidewalk. Budi is sitting with Mona, and the waiter comes over.

lines.speaker: الجرسون:
lines.id: Hi! What would you like to drink?

lines.speaker: منى:
lines.text: أنا عايزة شاي بالنعناع، من فضلك.
lines.literal: I want(f) tea with-the-mint, from your-kindness.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: وأنا عايز قهوة. مظبوط لو سمحت.
lines.id: And I'd like a coffee. Medium sweet, please.
lines.literal: and I want(m) coffee. exact if you-allow.

lines.speaker: منى:
lines.id: Could we also get a plate of kunafa to share?

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: I like it, but it's a bit strong for me.

lines.speaker: منى:
lines.id: Try the mint, then. You'll like it more.

lines.speaker: الجرسون:
lines.id: Here you are. The tea and the coffee.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: Thanks. How much is the bill, please?

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: Here you go. Keep the change.

notes: **The word عايز isn't a verb but an active participle (a verbal adjective).** That's why it never takes بـ and has no past tense. Only its form changes with the person: عايز for a man, عايزة for a woman, عايزين for a group. The spelling عاوز is also common and means exactly the same.

**The word ممكن is the safest way to open a request.** Literally "possible", it makes a request sound like an offer rather than an order. Compare هات المية (bring the water — sounds harsh) with ممكن مية؟ (could I have some water? — sounds polite).

**Notice that after ممكن the verb does NOT take بـ.** ممكن نتقاسمه, not ممكن بنتقاسمه. The same rule applies after عايز، لازم، ينفع, and it's one of foreign learners' biggest stumbling blocks. Full coverage in unit 13.
**The word حاضر means "certainly, right away" and is used by anyone accepting a request.** Waiters, drivers, shopkeepers, a friend you've asked a favor. It's much warmer than a plain طيب.
**The address يا فندم is a leftover from Turkish that survives in Egypt.** It's used for men and women alike, and also on its own as "pardon?" when you didn't hear what someone said.

**The word بقى has no fixed translation.** It's tossed onto the end of a sentence to add a gentle push or a conclusion — a bit like "then", "already", or "come on" in English. جرب بقى (go on, try it), يلا بقى (come on already), خلاص بقى (that's enough now).

**The phrase خليك بالباقي means "keep the change".** Tipping in Egypt isn't optional but part of the price: about ten percent in cafés and restaurants, and a few pounds for anyone who helps you. It's called بقشيش *ba’shiish*.

grammars.title: The word عايز and its three siblings
body: These are the four most important words for wanting, needing, having to, and being able to. Two of them change form; the other two never do.
after: The last two never change, whoever the person: أنا لازم أروح، هي لازم تروح، احنا لازم نروح. That makes them much easier to use, and beginners should lean on them first.
To negate them, put مش in front: مش عايز (don't want), مش لازم (no need), مش ممكن (impossible). Don't use the مـ...ـش wrapper here — none of the four is a verb.
After all four, the verb stands **without بـ**: عايز أشرب (want to drink), لازم تروح (you have to go), ممكن نقعد (may we sit). Remember this form without بـ well; this is the one place it's used.

grammars.title: Three levels of ordering
body: The same request can be said in three different tones, and choosing the right one matters more than vocabulary.

head: Tone
مصري
Say it
Meaning
rows: could I have some tea, please?
could I see the menu, please?

after: The blunt tone isn't rude in Egypt as long as it comes with a smile, and Egyptians use it themselves all the time. But for a foreigner, one level more polite is always the safer choice.
Two openers that are never wrong: لو سمحت at the **start** of the sentence, and من فضلك at the **end**. You can use both together.

blocks.text: Egyptian coffee is ordered by how much sugar it has, not by size, and it's one of the first things you need to decide: سادة *saada* with no sugar at all, عالريحة *‘ar-riiha* just a hint, مظبوط *mazbuuṭ* medium, زيادة *ziyaada* sweet. Ordering just قهوة without saying which will get you a question back from the waiter.

blocks.title: What an ahwa is, and what goes on there
items: The word قهوة means two things: coffee the drink, and the coffee shop itself. In Cairo, a قهوة is a street café with wooden chairs, little tables, a TV on, and people playing dominoes or backgammon for hours.
Ordering one glass of tea and sitting for two hours is normal and bothers no one. An Egyptian ahwa sells seats, not drinks.
The word شيشة *shiisha* (water pipe) is part of the scene too. If you don't want one, all you need is لأ شكراً، مابدخنش.

sections.title: Street food you have to try

blocks.text: Egypt has cheap, filling street food that's almost entirely plant-based. You'll see these names on the board outside every food stall.

head: مصري
Say it
What it is
rows: stewed spiced fava beans, the national breakfast
Egyptian falafel made from fava beans
rice, lentils, macaroni, tomato sauce, fried onions
thick green jute-leaf soup, typically Egyptian
pigeon stuffed with rice, a special dish

blocks.text: The word عيش is one of the best windows into the Egyptian soul: it means bread, but its root means "life". Bread isn't a side dish in Egypt but the very center of the meal, and Egyptians eat it with almost everything, rice included.

items: I'd like mint tea, please. (a woman speaking)
Could I see the menu, please?

exercises.prompt: Fill in the right form of عايز.
Make these requests more polite with ممكن or لو سمحت.
Put the words in the right order.

answers: أنا عايزة شاي بالنعناع، من فضلك. — ممكن المنيو لو سمحت؟ — كفاية كده، شكراً. — الحساب كام؟ — أنا مش عايز سكر.
ممكن مية لو سمحت؟ — الحساب من فضلك. — ممكن تفتح الشباك؟ — ممكن الملح لو سمحت؟ — ممكن تكلمني بكرة؟
أنا عايزة شاي من فضلك. — ممكن المنيو؟ — كفاية كده شكراً. — الحساب كام لو سمحت؟ — قهوة من غير سكر.
